newsitem.title: KENYA: Cenbank appeals to investors not to abandon Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Cenbank appeals to investors not to abandon Kenya.

text.p: Kenya's central bank governor Micah Cheserem on Friday appealed to foreign investors not to abandon east Africa's largest market following a decision by the International Monetary Fund's to halt a key aid package.

Cheserem spoke at a news conference a day after investors pulled out of Kenya's usually lucrative weekly auction of high-yield treasury bills citing market uncertainty. The row with the IMF has hurt the shilling and jolted investors.
The shillling has depreciated by 17 percent since the IMF decision on July 31, hitting its lowest official low since October 1993.
"The latest results of the treasury bill auction indicate that some foreign investors have decided to liquidate their investments and repatriate the proceeds," Cheserem said.
He added: "Kenya is still an attractive location considering the attractive interest rate it is paying. Our appeal is for investors to be patient as we resolve the current issues with the IMF."
